newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power rises on warmer weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power rises on warmer weather.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. rose Tuesday on warmer-than-expected weather after Hurricane Edouard spared much of the eastern seaboard this past weekend, industry sources said.
"Prices are up a little bit," said one typical regional trader.
But most players were quick to add overall power demand in the region is low, and will fall further as autumn approaches.
"The load factor is pretty low," said one utility trader.

In the New York Power Pool (NYPP), peak electricity prices for next-day delivery were quoted at $24.00-$25.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) with unconfirmed deals in the $24.50 area. NYPP peak prices were pegged in the range of $23.00-$24.00 late last week.
Next-day, off-peak power in NYPP was assessed at the $14.00 level, compared with late last week's range of $14.00-$16.00.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak power for Wednesday was discussed at $26.00-$26.50, up from $24.00-$25.00 late last week.
Next-day NEPOOL prices for off-peak hours were valued at $16.00-$17.00, down from $17.00-$18.00 late last week.

The Maine Yankee nuclear power plant is expected to resume normal output Wednesday after a six-week shutdown to investigate safety concerns. The 910 megawatt facility has been limited to operate at 90 percent of capacity by the federal Nuclear Regulatory Commission.
